-- @landing TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.SelfUniversal
-- @imports TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.UniversalStartup
-- @imports TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.CodeSimulator

/-!
# The self-application universal machine `U₀`

[AB09, Exercise 4.1] at self-application: one fixed machine `U₀` that, on an input
`pairEncode α w`, simulates the machine coded by `α` on that same input and reproduces its
output, with a space overhead that is a constant factor depending on `α` only. It is the
universal machine of `Complexity.space_hierarchy`'s window route (`machine-library-design.md`
§16b item 3): a public row built from H2's step block and H5's native device, not a private host
of that proof (`policy.md` §1, *Hosts come first*).

**Status: statement gate pending** (`audits/b6-hosts-statements-pack.md`). Both contracts are
sorried with their proof sketches.

## Design

* **Self-application.** The simulated input is all of `U₀`'s input, so the native device serves
  (`Turing.NativeAt`: its left boundary is a real blank) and no input position is stored or
  copied.
* **Forward only.** Halting runs within `s` cells are reproduced within `C_α · (s + 1)` cells;
  nothing is claimed of other runs, which is all the window route uses.
* **Library notions only.** The startup's endpoint is the step block's seam relation written
  out: the table on tape `1`, the unary initial state on tape `2` from cell `2`, the input head
  at `1`, the output empty. Neither statement names a declaration of the H2 promotion (H2-S), so
  its renaming changes only the sketches. The fill depends on H2-S round 2: the public step
  block contract, and the repaired iteration with its cofinality bound.
* **Generic in the effective scheme**; `Complexity.space_hierarchy` instantiates
  `Complexity.TimeHierarchy.code`.

## Main results

* `Turing.exists_selfStartupTM` — the startup, ending at the step block's seam (sorried).
* `Turing.exists_selfUniversal` — `U₀`, with its forward space ledger (sorried).

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.4.1, Theorem 1.9: the universal machine and its step;
  Exercise 4.1: the space-bounded universal machine; §4.1.3, proof of Theorem 4.8.)
-/

namespace Turing

/-- **`U₀`'s startup** (the RD-3 gate's check 2). For an effective scheme `c` there is a binary
machine with `K + 3` work tapes and an exit state such that for every code `α` there are a
time `T` and a space bound `B`, **depending on `α` only**, with the following property on every
input `pairEncode α w`. At time `T`, and not earlier, it is at its exit with:
* the input head at position `1`, `Cfg.init`'s position, and the output empty, having emitted
  nothing before (administrative output suppressed);
* tape `0`, the simulated work tape, blank, and tape `1` holding the canonical table
  `Turing.tableBitsK` of the decoded machine;
* tape `2` holding the decoded machine's initial state in unary from cell `2` (cells `0` and
  `1` blank), which is the step block's summary tape for an empty output;
* every other tape blank and every head at `0`.

Up to `T` it has visited at most `B` cells. This configuration is the step block's seam for
the decoded machine's initial configuration on the same input (H2's seam relation, private
`h1RoundRep` in `TuringMachine/CodeSimulator.lean`, at one coded work tape). [AB09, §1.4.1,
Theorem 1.9]

**Proof sketch.** Extract and canonize: `Turing.universalCanonTM c` (buffered composition of the
prefix parser and the canonizer), with its emissions captured on a scratch tape as in
`Turing.universalCaptureTM`; it ends after `3|α| + 4 + canonizerTime |α|` steps
(`Turing.universalCanon_complete`) with `serialize (decode α)` captured and the input head at
`2|α| + 3`. The serialization is `serializeK` (`Turing.oneTapeMachineFormat.serialize_eq`):
skip its doubled state count and separator, copy the unary initial state to tape `2` at offset
`2` and the remaining table to tape `1`; clear the scratch and the buffer. Rewind the input head
to position `1` (`Turing.FinTM.timed_rewind`, `2|α| + 5` steps). Every phase depends on `α`
only, so `T` and `B` do (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed_le_mul_succ` at the canonizer's halting
time bounds its cells). -/
theorem exists_selfStartupTM (c : EffectiveMachineCode) :
    ∃ (K : ℕ) (P : Type) (_ : Fintype P) (_ : DecidableEq P)
      (R : MultiTapeTM (K + 3) Bool P) (exit : P),
      ∀ α : List Bool, ∃ T B : ℕ, ∀ w : List Bool,
        R.runFrom (R.initCfg (pairEncode α w)) T =
          ⟨some exit, 1,
            fun j => if j = 1 then FinTM.bufferTape (tableBitsK (c.decode α).tm.tr)
              else if j = 2 then fun p => FinTM.bufferTape (unaryFin (c.decode α).tm.q₀) (p - 2)
              else fun _ => none,
            fun _ => 0, []⟩ ∧
        (∀ u < T, (R.runFrom (R.initCfg (pairEncode α w)) u).state ≠ some exit) ∧
        (∀ u ≤ T, (R.runFrom (R.initCfg (pairEncode α w)) u).output = []) ∧
        R.spaceUsed (R.initCfg (pairEncode α w)) T ≤ B := by
  sorry

/-- **`U₀`, the self-application universal machine** (`Complexity.space_hierarchy`'s sketch;
the sibling of `Complexity.space_universal`, with the native device in place of the
bounded-prefix one). For an effective scheme `c` there is a binary machine `U₀` such that
for every code `α` there is a constant `C > 0` with: whenever the machine coded by `α` halts
on `pairEncode α w` with some output, having visited at most `s` cells, `U₀` halts on the same
input with the same output, having visited at most `C · (s + 1)` cells. Only this forward
direction is claimed; `Complexity.space_hierarchy` instantiates
`c := Complexity.TimeHierarchy.code`. [AB09, Exercise 4.1, forward clause, at self-application;
§4.1.3, proof of Theorem 4.8]

Deviation: `C` depends on the code `α` (as in `Turing.universal`), and the input is the coded
machine's own input (self-application), so no copy and no position counter is needed.

**Proof sketch.** Startup, then wrapped rounds.
(i) *Startup.* `Turing.exists_selfStartupTM` reaches, within `B_α` cells, the step block's seam
for the coded machine's initial configuration on the same input: input head at `1`, table and
unary state in place, output empty.
(ii) *The wrapped round, with H2-S finding 4's reset invariant.* At every seam the step block's
bank represents the source configuration **with its output erased**, `{c with output := []}`
(so its summary cell is blank), while `U₀`'s own physical output is the real cumulative output
`c.output`. From such a seam at a live `c`, run H2's step block at one coded work tape, embedded
by R1 on tapes `0`–`2` (the public contract of the H2 promotion, `Turing.StepBlock.roundTM_effect`;
private `h1Round_effect` in `TuringMachine/CodeSimulator.lean` today), on `{c with output := []}`.
The transition read off the table depends only on the state, the input symbol and the work
symbol, which the erasure does not change, so the round ends at the seam of
`a.apply {c with output := []}`, with summary cell `summaryEmit none (a.output) = a.output`: the
round's exact emission. A host leaf on tape `2` then emits that bit, if any, so that `U₀`'s
output becomes `(a.apply c).output`, and blanks the cell, which re-establishes the invariant
for `a.apply c`. On the halting round the leaf runs before `U₀` halts physically (forwarding
precedes the halt).
(iii) *Iteration.* Induct on the source steps, as H2-S round 2's repaired `roundTM_iterate`
does (the additive iteration with the cofinality bound `t ≤ T`, H2-S finding 1), with each round
replaced by the wrapped round of (ii). Finding 4 notes that the silent iterate is not itself a
theorem about the wrapper, so the fill proves the wrapped iterate; it cites the repaired
`roundTM_iterate` directly if H2-S round 2 states it for a general round.
(iv) *Space.* In each round the mirrored head is at the source head's start or end cell and the
two auxiliary heads stay in `[-B, B]` with `B := 50·(|tableBitsK| + 1)` (`roundTM_visited`); the
leaf moves no head. So the mirrored tape visits only cells the coded machine visits, at most `s`;
the auxiliary tapes at most `2B + 1` cells each; the startup `B_α`. The space is at most
`B_α + s + 2(2B + 1) ≤ C_α · (s + 1)`. -/
theorem exists_selfUniversal (c : EffectiveMachineCode) :
    ∃ U₀ : FinTM Bool, ∀ α : List Bool, ∃ C : ℕ, 0 < C ∧
      ∀ (w output : List Bool) (t s : ℕ),
        (c.decode α).toFinTM.ComputesInTime (pairEncode α w) output t →
        (c.decode α).toFinTM.tm.spaceUsed
            ((c.decode α).toFinTM.tm.initCfg (pairEncode α w)) t ≤ s →
          ∃ t' : ℕ, U₀.ComputesInTime (pairEncode α w) output t' ∧
            U₀.tm.spaceUsed (U₀.tm.initCfg (pairEncode α w)) t' ≤ C * (s + 1) := by
  sorry

end Turing

/-! ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Part K · replaces the declaration `Complexity.space_universal` (docstring and statement) in
`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Hierarchy` (`SpaceComplexity/Hierarchy.lean`), without the
namespace lines (user decision B1, 2026-10-13). The statement differs from the gated one only
in its last line, `C * s` for `C * (s + logSpace x.length + 1)`; the probe
`GatedFormProbe.lean` derives the gated statement from it. The module docstring and one
sentence of `Complexity.space_hierarchy`'s docstring change with it (patch
`Hierarchy.patch`). -/
-- @landing TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Hierarchy
-- @place replace theorem space_universal :
-- @imports TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ConfigGraph
-- @imports TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Constructible
-- @imports TCSlib.Complexity.TimeHierarchy.CodePrefix TCSlib.Complexity.TimeHierarchy.Diagonal
-- @imports TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.NP

namespace Complexity

open Turing

/-- **The space-bounded universal machine** ([AB09, Exercise 4.1], p. 93,
forward clause; spec, fill pending — phase P4.3, restated forward-only
2026-10-12 by design §16b item 3, RD-3 statement gate passed 2026-10-13;
strengthened to the addend-free `C · s` 2026-10-13, statement gate pending):
for the fixed scheme there is a machine `SU` such that for every code `α`
there is a constant `C > 0` with: whenever the coded machine halts on `x`
with `output`, having visited at most `s` work cells by then, `SU` on input
`⟨bits s, ⟨α, x⟩⟩` halts with the same `output`, having visited at most
`C · s` work cells: the book's `C · t`. Nothing is claimed when the coded
machine overruns `s` or does not halt. The time is existential, as
`Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime`'s halting demands, with no stated bound. Every
qualifying run has `s ≥ 1` (`Turing.CodeTM.one_le_spaceUsed`), so the bound
is never `0`.

Deviations from the book's `SU(α, t, x) = M_α(x)` within `C · t` cells:
* **`C` depends on the representation `α`**, not only on `M_α`, as in
  `Turing.universal`, whose module docstring records why an arbitrary
  effective scheme forces this.
* "Halts before using `t` cells" is read as "at most `s` visited cells"; the
  budget is an argument of `SU`, as in the book, but is never read.
* The output is the simulated output itself: with no failure clause there is
  no verdict to tag. The former `[false]` clause, and with it the
  visited-interval counters, the core-count clock and the probe/replay of the
  previous statement, went with design §16b item 3.

There is no input-device addend: the gated `+ logSpace |x| + 1` (a binary
position for the simulated input head) is replaced by a unary ruler of the
header's length, whose cells the bound absorbs (the RD-3 gate's minor 1).

**Proof sketch.** A code-first interpreter in three parts. (i) **Startup.**
Parse the header `bits s`, `α` and the two separators by a finite-state pair
scan, writing one ruler cell per header cell, so that the ruler is `true^ℓ`
with `ℓ = 2|bits s| + 2|α| + 4` (`Turing.pairEncode_pairEncode_length`,
`Turing.pairEncode_pairEncode_drop`) and the physical input head ends at
`ℓ + 1`, the virtual position `1`; the budget is never read. Canonize `α`
into the table and state tapes as `U₀`'s startup does
(`Turing.exists_selfStartupTM`'s phases, reading the code where the header
holds it). Its cells are a constant depending only on `α`
(`Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed_le_mul_succ` at the canonizer's halting time);
the effective scheme supplies no bound linear in `|α|`, and none is claimed.
(ii) **Input device and step block** (H5's bounded-prefix ruler device and
H2). Run `U₀`'s wrapped round loop (`Turing.exists_selfUniversal`'s sketch:
H2's step block on the output-erased source, with the leaf that forwards each
emission before the next round and before the halt) through the ruler host
`Turing.exists_rulerHostTM` on the virtual input `x`. The host is a positive
finite block simulation: it reads a blank and suppresses left moves at the
virtual left boundary, which it tests by restoring sweeps of `ℓ` cells
(`Turing.exists_rulerTestTM`), so `SU` halts exactly when the round loop does,
with its output, the coded machine's. The chapter-1 interpreter's device
cannot serve: its fourth tape holds a unary boundary marker whose head
`applyRecord` moves with the input head (`Turing.universalInterpreter`), so
that tape uses one plus the largest simulated input position reached,
`Θ(|x| + 1)` cells on a full scan, which a budget `s = o(|x|)` does not
cover (Finding B). (iii) **Space.** The host's bank visits exactly the round
loop's cells: the mirrored tape only the coded machine's, at most `s`, and the
table and summary tapes `O(|table| + 1)`, a constant for fixed `α`. Its ruler
visits `ℓ + 2` cells. Every qualifying run has `s ≥ 1`
(`Turing.CodeTM.one_le_spaceUsed`) and `|bits s| ≤ s`
(`Turing.length_bits_le_self`), so `ℓ ≤ 2s + 2|α| + 4 ≤ (2|α| + 6) · s`, and
the total `C_α + s + ℓ + 2` is at most `C · s`. Fill obligations, named: the
header-ruler startup with the buffered canonization; the H5 ruler host;
`U₀`'s wrapped round loop (H2 at one coded work tape, with its head
envelope); the per-code constant ledger. -/
theorem space_universal :
    ∃ SU : FinTM Bool, ∀ α : List Bool, ∃ C : ℕ, 0 < C ∧
      ∀ (s : ℕ) (x output : List Bool) (t : ℕ),
        ((TimeHierarchy.code).decode α).toFinTM.ComputesInTime x output t →
        ((TimeHierarchy.code).decode α).toFinTM.tm.spaceUsed
            (((TimeHierarchy.code).decode α).toFinTM.tm.initCfg x) t ≤ s →
          ∃ t' : ℕ,
            SU.ComputesInTime (pairEncode (Nat.bits s) (pairEncode α x)) output t' ∧
            SU.tm.spaceUsed
                (SU.tm.initCfg (pairEncode (Nat.bits s) (pairEncode α x))) t'
              ≤ C * s := by
  sorry

end Complexity

/-! Probe (evidence only): the landing form's step clock implies the draft's statement, which the
C1 pack cites. The statement below is the draft's, extracted verbatim and renamed. -/

namespace Turing

theorem exists_stepClockTMVia_draft_form {k : ℕ} {Γ S : Type} [Fintype S] [DecidableEq S]
    [DecidableEq Γ] (e : Bool ↪ Γ) (M : MultiTapeTM k Γ S) (stopAt : S → Bool) :
    ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Fintype Q) (_ : DecidableEq Q) (H : MultiTapeTM (k + 1) Γ Q)
      (inj : S → Q) (finish timeout : Option S → Q),
      Function.Injective finish ∧ Function.Injective timeout ∧
      (∀ a b, finish a ≠ timeout b) ∧ (∀ s r, inj s ≠ finish r ∧ inj s ≠ timeout r) ∧
      ∀ {x : List Γ} (c : Cfg k Γ S x) (q : S), c.state = some q →
      ∀ (w : List Bool) (ct : ℤ → Option Γ) (cp : ℤ),
        (∀ p : ℤ, -1 ≤ p → p ≤ (w.length : ℤ) → ct (cp + p) = FinTM.bufferTape (w.map e) p) →
        (∀ τ ≤ Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat), (M.runFrom c τ).Stopped stopAt →
          (∀ u < τ, ¬(M.runFrom c u).Stopped stopAt) →
          ∃ T ≤ 5 * τ + 2 * w.length + 2, ∃ w' : List Bool, w'.length = w.length ∧
            H.runFrom (clockCfg (some (inj q)) c ct cp) T =
              clockCfg (some (finish (M.runFrom c τ).state)) (M.runFrom c τ)
                (wordPatch ct cp (w'.map e)) cp ∧
            (∀ u < T, ∀ r,
              (H.runFrom (clockCfg (some (inj q)) c ct cp) u).state ≠ some (finish r) ∧
              (H.runFrom (clockCfg (some (inj q)) c ct cp) u).state ≠ some (timeout r)) ∧
            ∀ u ≤ T, ∃ v ≤ τ,
              (∀ j : Fin k, (H.runFrom (clockCfg (some (inj q)) c ct cp) u).workTapePos
                j.castSucc = (M.runFrom c v).workTapePos j) ∧
              (H.runFrom (clockCfg (some (inj q)) c ct cp) u).workTapePos (Fin.last k) ∈
                Finset.Icc (cp - 1) (cp + (w.length : ℤ))) ∧
        ((∀ u ≤ Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat), ¬(M.runFrom c u).Stopped stopAt) →
          ∃ T ≤ 5 * Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat) + 2 * w.length + 2,
            ∃ w' : List Bool, w'.length = w.length ∧
            H.runFrom (clockCfg (some (inj q)) c ct cp) T =
              clockCfg (some (timeout (M.runFrom c (Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat))).state))
                (M.runFrom c (Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat)))
                (wordPatch ct cp (w'.map e)) cp ∧
            (∀ u < T, ∀ r,
              (H.runFrom (clockCfg (some (inj q)) c ct cp) u).state ≠ some (finish r) ∧
              (H.runFrom (clockCfg (some (inj q)) c ct cp) u).state ≠ some (timeout r)) ∧
            ∀ u ≤ T, ∃ v ≤ Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat),
              (∀ j : Fin k, (H.runFrom (clockCfg (some (inj q)) c ct cp) u).workTapePos
                j.castSucc = (M.runFrom c v).workTapePos j) ∧
              (H.runFrom (clockCfg (some (inj q)) c ct cp) u).workTapePos (Fin.last k) ∈
                Finset.Icc (cp - 1) (cp + (w.length : ℤ))) := by
  obtain ⟨Q, hQ, dQ, H, inj, finish, timeout, h1, h2, h3, h4, h⟩ :=
    exists_stepClockTMVia e M stopAt
  refine ⟨Q, hQ, dQ, H, inj, finish, timeout, h1, h2, h3, h4, ?_⟩
  intro x c q hq w ct cp hw
  obtain ⟨hf, ht⟩ := h c q hq w ct cp hw
  refine ⟨fun τ hτ hs hm => ?_, fun hn => ?_⟩
  · obtain ⟨T, hT, w', hw', hr, hc, hfr⟩ := hf τ hτ hs hm
    refine ⟨T, hT, w', hw', hr, hc, fun u hu => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨v, hv, hj, -, -, hcp⟩ := hfr u hu
    exact ⟨v, hv, fun j => (hj j).2, hcp⟩
  · obtain ⟨T, hT, w', hw', hr, hc, hfr⟩ := ht hn
    refine ⟨T, hT, w', hw', hr, hc, fun u hu => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨v, hv, hj, -, -, hcp⟩ := hfr u hu
    exact ⟨v, hv, fun j => (hj j).2, hcp⟩

end Turing

## ===== audits/evidence/b6hosts/gate/scripts/gate.py =====

```
"""B6 hosts statement gate: landing and cut checks (read-only on the worktree; standard library).

Usage:
  python3 -I gate.py land <unit.lean> <worktree> <edits.py> <outdir>
  python3 -I gate.py cut  <unit.lean> <worktree> <edits.py> <outdir>

The unit is split into parts at header lines starting with HEADER. Each part names its landing
module (`-- @landing M`), its placement for an existing module (`-- @place append`,
`-- @place insert-before <line prefix>`, `-- @place insert-after <line>`,
`-- @place replace <declaration line>`) and its imports (`-- @imports a b ...`, possibly several
lines). The part's body is everything after its last marker line up to the next header.

`land` writes <outdir>/landing/<path> for every new module (copyright block, the part's imports,
the standard options, the part verbatim) and <outdir>/patched/<path> for every existing module
touched (the part placed as its header says, then the asserted edits of <edits.py>, each of
which must match exactly once), and <outdir>/patches/<File>.patch is left to `diff -u`.

`cut` writes <outdir>/cut/<Module>.check.lean for every part and <outdir>/cut/<File>.patched.
check.lean for every patched existing module: the imports of the target and of the parts in
its import closure, the standard options, the bodies of those parts in file order, then the
target's own body. The import closure is computed over the worktree's import graph, so a part
appended to an existing module is included wherever that module is (transitively) imported. A
`replace` part is never included in another target (it would clash with the snapshot's own
declaration); no Lean declaration consumes the replaced theorem.
"""
import os
import re
import sys

HEADER = "/-! ════"
COPYRIGHT = """/-
Copyright (c) 2026 Seyoon Ragavan. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
"""
OPTIONS = """set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false
"""


def rd(p):
    return open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()


def wr(p, s):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True)
    open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s)


def mod_path(m):
    return os.path.join(*m.split(".")) + ".lean"


def exists(wt, m):
    if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(wt, mod_path(m))):
        return True
    pk = os.path.join(wt, ".lake", "packages")
    return any(os.path.isfile(os.path.join(pk, d, mod_path(m))) for d in os.listdir(pk))


def graph(wt):
    g = {}
    for dp, _, fs in os.walk(os.path.join(wt, "TCSlib")):
        for f in fs:
            if f.endswith(".lean"):
                p = os.path.join(dp, f)
                m = os.path.relpath(p, wt)[:-5].replace(os.sep, ".")
                g[m] = [l.split()[1] for l in rd(p).split("\n") if l.startswith("import TCSlib")]
    g["TCSlib"] = [l.split()[1] for l in rd(os.path.join(wt, "TCSlib.lean")).split("\n")
                   if l.startswith("import TCSlib")]
    return g


def parse(unit):
    lines = rd(unit).split("\n")
    first_doc = next(i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith("/-!"))
    head = [l.split()[1] for l in lines[:first_doc] if l.startswith("import ")]
    starts = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith(HEADER)]
    parts = []
    for n, s in enumerate(starts):
        e = starts[n + 1] if n + 1 < len(starts) else len(lines)
        block = lines[s:e]
        land = [l.split()[2] for l in block if l.startswith("-- @landing ")]
        place = [l[len("-- @place "):] for l in block if l.startswith("-- @place ")]
        imps = [w for l in block if l.startswith("-- @imports ") for w in l.split()[2:]]
        last = max(i for i, l in enumerate(block) if l.startswith("-- @"))
        assert len(land) == 1 and len(place) <= 1, f"part at line {s + 1}"
        body = "\n".join(block[last + 1:]).strip("\n") + "\n"
        parts.append({"land": land[0], "place": place[0] if place else None, "imports": imps,
                      "body": body, "line": s + 1, "label": chr(ord("A") + n)})
    return head, parts


def inner(body):
    ls = body.strip("\n").split("\n")
    while ls and (re.match(r"^(namespace \S+|open .*)$", ls[0]) or not ls[0].strip()):
        ls.pop(0)
    while ls and (re.match(r"^end \S+$", ls[-1]) or not ls[-1].strip()):
        ls.pop()
    return "\n".join(ls) + "\n"


def place(orig, p):
    kind, _, arg = p["place"].partition(" ")
    ls = orig.split("\n")
    if kind == "append":
        return orig.rstrip("\n") + "\n\n" + p["body"]
    if kind == "insert-before":
        idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(ls) if l.startswith(arg)]
        assert len(idx) == 1, (p["land"], kind, idx)
        i = idx[0]
        return "\n".join(ls[:i]) + "\n" + inner(p["body"]) + "\n" + "\n".join(ls[i:])
    if kind == "insert-after":
        idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(ls) if l == arg]
        assert len(idx) == 1, (p["land"], kind, idx)
        i = idx[0] + 1
        return "\n".join(ls[:i]) + "\n\n" + inner(p["body"]).rstrip("\n") + "\n" + \
            "\n".join(ls[i:])
    if kind == "replace":
        idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(ls) if l == arg]
        assert len(idx) == 1, (p["land"], kind, idx)
        a = idx[0]
        d0 = max(i for i in range(a) if ls[i].startswith("/--"))
        assert not any(re.match(r"^(theorem|lemma|def) ", ls[i]) for i in range(d0, a))
        e = next(i for i in range(a, len(ls)) if ls[i] == "  sorry")
        return "\n".join(ls[:d0]) + "\n" + inner(p["body"]).rstrip("\n") + "\n" + \
            "\n".join(ls[e + 1:])
    raise SystemExit(f"unknown placement {kind}")


def load_edits(path):
    ns = {}
    exec(compile(rd(path), path, "exec"), ns)
    return ns["EDITS"]


def apply_edits(text, edits, name):
    for k, (old, new) in enumerate(edits):
        n = text.count(old)
        assert n == 1, f"{name}: edit {k} matches {n} times: {old[:60]!r}"
        text = text.replace(old, new)
    return text


def land(unit, wt, edits_path, out):
    head, parts = parse(unit)
    edits = load_edits(edits_path)
    news = {p["land"] for p in parts if not exists(wt, p["land"])}
    touched = {}
    for p in parts:
        path = mod_path(p["land"])
        if p["land"] in news:
            assert p["place"] is None, p["land"]
            imps = "".join(f"import {m}\n" for m in p["imports"])
            wr(os.path.join(out, "landing", path), COPYRIGHT + imps + "\n" + OPTIONS + "\n" + p["body"])
            print(f"new      {path}: part {p['label']}")
        else:
            assert p["place"], p["land"]
            src = touched.get(path, rd(os.path.join(wt, path)))
            touched[path] = place(src, p)
            print(f"placed   {path}: part {p['label']} ({p['place'].split()[0]})")
    for path, es in edits.items():
        src = touched.get(path, rd(os.path.join(wt, path)))
        touched[path] = apply_edits(src, es, path)
        print(f"edited   {path}: {len(es)} asserted edits")
    for path, text in touched.items():
        wr(os.path.join(out, "patched", path), text)
    return parts


def closure(g, mods, part_by_land, news):
    seen, todo = set(), list(mods)
    while todo:
        m = todo.pop()
        if m in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(m)
        if m in news:
            todo += part_by_land[m]["imports"]
        else:
            todo += g.get(m, [])
    return seen


def check_file(imps, bodies):
    return COPYRIGHT + "".join(f"import {m}\n" for m in imps) + "\n" + OPTIONS + "\n" + \
        "\n".join(b.rstrip("\n") + "\n" for b in bodies)


def cut(unit, wt, edits_path, out):
    head, parts = parse(unit)
    g = graph(wt)
    news = {p["land"] for p in parts if not exists(wt, p["land"])}
    by_land = {p["land"]: p for p in parts}
    assert len(by_land) == len(parts), "one part per landing module"
    union = []
    for p in parts:
        for m in p["imports"]:
            if m not in news and m not in union:
                union.append(m)
    print(f"unit imports: {len(head)}; union of the parts' existing imports: {len(union)}; "
          f"missing from unit: {[m for m in union if m not in head]}; "
          f"extra in unit: {[m for m in head if m not in union]}")
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(out, "cut"), exist_ok=True)

    def target(name, imps, own, body):
        clo = closure(g, imps, by_land, news)
        inc = [q for q in parts if q is not own and q["land"] in clo
               and (q["place"] is None or not q["place"].startswith("replace"))
               and not (own is not None and own["place"] is None and q["land"] == own["land"])]
        allimps = []
        for m in imps + [m for q in inc for m in q["imports"]]:
            if m not in news and m not in allimps:
                allimps.append(m)
        wr(os.path.join(out, "cut", name), check_file(allimps, [q["body"] for q in inc] + [body]))
        labels = ",".join(q["label"] for q in inc)
        print(f"{name}: parts [{labels}] + own; imports {len(allimps)}")

    for p in parts:
        target(p["land"] + ".check.lean", p["imports"], p, p["body"])
    edits = load_edits(edits_path)
    patched_paths = sorted({mod_path(p["land"]) for p in parts if p["land"] not in news} |
                           set(edits))
    for path in patched_paths:
        text = rd(os.path.join(out, "patched", path))
        ls = text.split("\n")
        imps = [l.split()[1] for l in ls if l.startswith("import ")]
        doc = next(i for i, l in enumerate(ls) if l.startswith("/-!"))
        k = max([i for i in range(doc) if ls[i].startswith("set_option ")] or
                [i for i in range(doc) if ls[i].startswith("import ")])
        body = "\n".join(ls[k + 1:]).strip("\n") + "\n"
        m = path[:-5].replace(os.sep, ".")
        own = by_land.get(m)
        target(os.path.basename(path)[:-5] + ".patched.check.lean", imps,
               own if own is not None else {"place": "self", "land": m}, body)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    cmd, unit, wt, edits_path, out = sys.argv[1:6]
    if cmd == "land":
        land(unit, wt, edits_path, out)
    elif cmd == "cut":
        cut(unit, wt, edits_path, out)
    else:
        raise SystemExit("usage: land|cut")
```

"""The asserted edits of the B6 hosts landing, beyond the placed parts (read by gate.py).

Each entry is (old, new); gate.py asserts that `old` occurs exactly once in the file after the
parts are placed, then replaces it. Paths are relative to the worktree root.

TM = "TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/"
SC = "TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/"

EDITS = {}

# StateRenaming: the module docstring lists the two new results.
EDITS[TM + "StateRenaming.lean"] = [

  at every time.
""",

  at every time.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.relabelState_visitedByTapeHead`,
  `Turing.MultiTapeTM.relabelState_spaceUsed` — so do head trajectories and space at
  every time (the space clause of the coding step).
"""),
]

# Encoding: the module docstring lists the new results; `exists_codeTM` becomes the time clause
# of `exists_codeTM_spaceUsed` (statement unchanged), so that the relabelling is built once.
EDITS[TM + "Encoding.lean"] = [
    ("""* `Turing.exists_codeTM` — every one-work-tape binary machine is equivalent to a
  coded machine (state relabeling).
""",
     """* `Turing.exists_codeTM` — every one-work-tape binary machine is equivalent to a
  coded machine (state relabeling).
* `Turing.exists_codeTM_spaceUsed` — the same coded machine also uses the same space at
  every time; `Turing.CodeTM.one_le_spaceUsed` — every coded run visits a cell.
"""),
    ("""The implementation uses `Turing.MultiTapeTM.relabelState` (the shared state-renaming
module, `TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.StateRenaming`), eliminates `hk` after
destructuring the bundle, and concludes with
`Turing.MultiTapeTM.relabelState_runFrom_init`. -/
theorem exists_codeTM (M : FinTM Bool) (hk : M.k = 1) :
    ∃ M' : CodeTM, ∀ (x output : List Bool) (t : ℕ),
      M'.toFinTM.ComputesInTime x output t ↔ M.ComputesInTime x output t := by
  classical
  rcases M with @⟨k, Q, hQ, dQ, tm⟩
  dsimp only at hk
  subst k
  letI : Fintype Q := hQ
  letI : DecidableEq Q := dQ
  have hcard : Fintype.card Q = (Fintype.card Q - 1) + 1 := by
    have : 0 < Fintype.card Q := Fintype.card_pos_iff.mpr ⟨tm.q₀⟩
    omega
  let e := Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq hcard
  refine ⟨⟨Fintype.card Q - 1, tm.relabelState e⟩, ?_⟩
  intro x output t
  simp only [CodeTM.toFinTM, FinTM.ComputesInTime, MultiTapeTM.ComputesInTimeAndSpace,
    MultiTapeTM.relabelState_runFrom_init, Cfg.mapState, Option.map_eq_none_iff]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨s, hhalt, hout, -⟩
    exact ⟨_, hhalt, hout, rfl⟩
  · rintro ⟨s, hhalt, hout, -⟩
    exact ⟨_, hhalt, hout, rfl⟩
""",
     """The implementation is the time clause of `Turing.exists_codeTM_spaceUsed`, whose witness
is this relabelling (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.relabelState`, from the shared state-renaming module
`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.StateRenaming`), so that the relabelling is built once. -/
theorem exists_codeTM (M : FinTM Bool) (hk : M.k = 1) :
    ∃ M' : CodeTM, ∀ (x output : List Bool) (t : ℕ),
      M'.toFinTM.ComputesInTime x output t ↔ M.ComputesInTime x output t := by
  obtain ⟨M', h, -⟩ := exists_codeTM_spaceUsed M hk
  exact ⟨M', h⟩
"""),
]

# ConfigCount: the module docstring lists the new results.
EDITS[SC + "ConfigCount.lean"] = [

* `Complexity.LOGSPACE_subset_P`""",

* `Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.spaceUsed_le_of_halt`,
  `Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace.computesFunInTime_and_forall_spaceUsed_le` — the halt-time

* `Turing.FinTM.decidesInSpace_of_alphabetReduction` — a rich-alphabet machine deciding on the
  `Bool` inputs within an all-input space bound gives a `SPACE` decider. [AB09, Claim 1.5]
* `Complexity.LOGSPACE_subset_P`"""),

private def sumCode : OutSummary → Fin 3
  | .empty => 0
  | .accept => 1
  | .dead => 2

/-- Distinct summaries have distinct three-element codes. -/
private theorem sumCode_injective : Function.Injective sumCode := by
  intro a b h
  cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all [sumCode]

""", ""),
    ("""  let code j := (MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.coreCode s (cs j), sumCode (outSummary (cs j).output))
""",
     """  let code j :=
    (MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.coreCode s (cs j), outSummaryCode (outSummary (cs j).output))
"""),
    ("""    · exact sumCode_injective (congrArg Prod.snd eqcode)
""",
     """    · exact outSummaryCode_injective (congrArg Prod.snd eqcode)
"""),
    ("""/-- The canonical rich record of a graph vertex, using S1a's summary code.
""",
     """/-- The canonical rich record of a graph vertex, using the summary code `Turing.outSummaryCode`.
"""),
    ("""  cfgRecord s c (sumCode (outSummary c.output))
""",
     """  cfgRecord s c (outSummaryCode (outSummary c.output))
"""),
    ("""and the tag. S1a's injective `sumCode` recovers the output summary. -/
""",
     """and the tag. The injective `Turing.outSummaryCode` recovers the output summary. -/
"""),
    ("""    sumCode_injective.eq_iff]
""",
     """    outSummaryCode_injective.eq_iff]
"""),
    ("""/-- Representatives of the three summary codes, used only to compute tag
updates. The encoding itself is the received `sumCode`. -/
private def s1b_summaryWord (τ : Fin 3) : List Bool :=
  if τ = sumCode .empty then [] else if τ = sumCode .accept then [true] else [false]

/-- Each chosen representative has the requested summary code.

**Proof sketch.** Check the three elements of `Fin 3`; the existing encoding
computes on the empty, accepting and dead representative words. -/
private theorem s1b_summaryWord_code (τ : Fin 3) :
    sumCode (outSummary (s1b_summaryWord τ)) = τ := by
  fin_cases τ <;> rfl

/-- The record-step tag update is summary append on a representative word. -/
private def s1b_tagUpdate (τ : Fin 3) (b : Option Bool) : Fin 3 :=
  sumCode (outSummary (s1b_summaryWord τ ++ b.toList))

/-- An absent emission preserves the tag, as required by `recordStepTM`.

**Proof sketch.** Appending no symbol preserves the representative word. -/
private theorem s1b_tagUpdate_none (τ : Fin 3) : s1b_tagUpdate τ none = τ := by
  simpa [s1b_tagUpdate] using s1b_summaryWord_code τ

/-- The finite tag update agrees with every actual output history.

**Proof sketch.** The representative and actual word have equal summaries
by injectivity of S1a's code. Apply its append-congruence theorem. -/
private theorem s1b_tagUpdate_output (u : List Bool) (b : Option Bool) :
    s1b_tagUpdate (sumCode (outSummary u)) b = sumCode (outSummary (u ++ b.toList)) := by
  exact congrArg sumCode (outSummary_append_congr

## ===== audits/evidence/b6hosts/gate/scripts/freeze.py =====

```
"""Freeze check for patched existing files (read-only; standard library only).

Usage: python3 -I freeze.py [--report] <original.lean> <patched.lean>
       [allowed-statement-changes] [allowed-body-changes]

Each file is cut into declarations (with their namespaces). For every declaration the
docstring, the statement (the comment-stripped text after the declared name up to the proof's
`:=`, a ` where`, or the first match arm; a `:=` on a line with `let` or `have` belongs to the
statement) and the body (the comment-stripped rest) are compared, whitespace-collapsed.
Reports: declarations added and removed (public and private separately), and for each kept
declaration whether its statement, body or docstring changed. A statement or body change not
listed in the allowance arguments (comma-separated full names) is flagged UNAUTHORIZED; the
exit status is 1 if anything is flagged. The module docstring and other comments outside
declarations are reported as one item.
"""
import re
import sys

DECL = re.compile(r"^(?:@\[[^\]]*\]\s*)*((?:(?:private|protected|noncomputable|nonrec|partial)\s+)*)"
                  r"(theorem|lemma|def|abbrev|instance|structure|inductive|class)\s+([^\s(:{\[]+)?")
STOP = re.compile(r"^(end\b|namespace\b|section\b|open\b|variable\b|set_option\b|#|attribute\b|"
                  r"universe\b|noncomputable section\b)")


def split_comments(src):
    """Return (code with comments blanked, list of (start, end, text, is_doc) comments)."""
    out, comments, i, n = [], [], 0, len(src)
    while i < n:
        if src.startswith("/-", i):
            depth, j = 1, i + 2
            while j < n and depth:
                if src.startswith("/-", j):
                    depth += 1; j += 2
                elif src.startswith("-/", j):
                    depth -= 1; j += 2
                else:
                    j += 1
            comments.append((i, j, src[i:j], src.startswith("/--", i)))
            out.append("".join(c if c == "\n" else " " for c in src[i:j]))
            i = j
        elif src.startswith("--", i):
            j = src.find("\n", i)
            j = n if j < 0 else j
            out.append(" " * (j - i))
            i = j
        else:
            out.append(src[i]); i += 1
    return "".join(out), comments


def decls(src):
    code, comments = split_comments(src)
    lines = code.split("\n")
    offs, o = [], 0
    for l in lines:
        offs.append(o); o += len(l) + 1
    docs = {c[1]: c[2] for c in comments if c[3]}
    stack, res, cur = [], [], None

    def close(endline):
        nonlocal cur
        if cur:
            text = "\n".join(lines[cur["line"]:endline])
            res.append(dict(cur, text=text))
        cur = None

    for i, l in enumerate(lines):
        m = DECL.match(l)
        if m and not l.startswith(" "):
            close(i)
            name = m.group(3) or "<anon>"
            full = name[len("_root_."):] if name.startswith("_root_.") else \
                ".".join([s for k, s in stack if k == "ns"] + [name])
            # the docstring that ends right before this line
            doc = ""
            for (a, b, t, isdoc) in comments:
                if isdoc and b <= offs[i] and not src[b:offs[i]].strip():
                    doc = t
            cur = {"name": full, "private": "private" in m.group(1), "line": i, "doc": doc}
            continue
        s = l.strip()
        if STOP.match(l):
            close(i)
            mm = re.match(r"^namespace\s+(\S+)", l)
            if mm:
                for part in mm.group(1).split("."):
                    stack.append(("ns", part))
            mm = re.match(r"^(?:noncomputable\s+)?section\b\s*(\S*)", l)
            if mm:
                stack.append(("sec", mm.group(1)))
            mm = re.match(r"^end\b\s*(\S*)", l)
            if mm:
                nm = mm.group(1)
                if nm:
                    for part in reversed(nm.split(".")):
                        if stack and stack[-1][1] == part:
                            stack.pop()
                elif stack and stack[-1][0] == "sec":
                    stack.pop()
    close(len(lines))
    out = {}
    for d in res:
        t = d["text"]
        hm = DECL.match(t)  # drop the keyword and the declared name: compare from the binders on
        t = t[hm.end():] if hm else t
        mm = None
        for cand in re.finditer(r":=|\swhere\b|\n\s*\|", t):
            line = t[t.rfind("\n", 0, cand.start()) + 1:cand.start()]
            if cand.group(0) == ":=" and re.search(r"\b(let|have)\b", line):
                continue  # a `let`/`have` inside the statement, not the proof's `:=`
            mm = cand
            break
        stmt, body = (t[:mm.start()], t[mm.start():]) if mm else (t, "")
        key = d["name"]
        while key in out:
            key += "'"
        out[key] = {"private": d["private"], "stmt": " ".join(stmt.split()),
                    "body": " ".join(body.split()), "doc": " ".join(d["doc"].split())}
    return out, " ".join(" ".join(c[2] for c in comments if not c[3]).split())


def main():
    report = "--report" in sys.argv
    if report:
        sys.argv.remove("--report")
    a_src, b_src = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read(), open(sys.argv[2],
                                                                     encoding="utf-8").read()
    allow_stmt = set(sys.argv[3].split(",")) if len(sys.argv) > 3 and sys.argv[3] else set()
    allow_body = set(sys.argv[4].split(",")) if len(sys.argv) > 4 and sys.argv[4] else set()
    A, ca = decls(a_src)
    B, cb = decls(b_src)
    bad = 0
    pubA = {n for n in A if not A[n]["private"]}
    pubB = {n for n in B if not B[n]["private"]}
    privA, privB = set(A) - pubA, set(B) - pubB
    print(f"declarations before/after: {len(A)}/{len(B)} (public {len(pubA)}/{len(pubB)}, "
          f"private {len(privA)}/{len(privB)})")
    print("public added:", sorted(pubB - pubA))
    print("public removed:", sorted(pubA - pubB))
    print("private added:", sorted(privB - privA))
    print("private removed:", sorted(privA - privB))
    for n in sorted(set(A) & set(B)):
        a, b = A[n], B[n]
        flags = []
        if a["stmt"] != b["stmt"]:
            ok = n in allow_stmt
            flags.append("statement changed" + (" (authorized)" if ok else " UNAUTHORIZED"))
            bad += not ok
        if a["body"] != b["body"]:
            ok = n in allow_body
            flags.append("body changed" + (" (authorized)" if ok else " UNAUTHORIZED"))
            bad += not ok
        if a["doc"] != b["doc"]:
            flags.append("docstring changed")
        if a["private"] != b["private"]:
            flags.append("visibility changed UNAUTHORIZED")
            bad += 1
        if flags:
            print(f"  {n}{' (private)' if a['private'] else ''}: " + "; ".join(flags))
    unchanged = sum(1 for n in set(A) & set(B) if A[n] == B[n])
    print(f"kept declarations byte-identical (comment-stripped statement, body, docstring): "
          f"{unchanged} of {len(set(A) & set(B))}")
    print("other comments (module docstring, section headers):",
          "unchanged" if ca == cb else "changed")
    for n in allow_stmt | allow_body:
        if n and n not in A:
            print(f"  allowance names an unknown declaration: {n}")
            bad += 1
    if report:
        print(f"RESULT: comparison only; {bad} difference(s) outside the allowances")
        return
    print("RESULT:", "PASS" if bad == 0 else f"FAIL ({bad})")
    sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

## ===== audits/evidence/b6hosts/gate/scripts/names.py =====

```
"""Name screen (read-only): the declarations of the gate unit, with their namespaces, against
every declaration of the worktree's TCSlib tree.

Usage: python3 -I names.py <unit.lean> [more units ...] <worktree> [--list <out.txt>]

Reports full-name clashes (a clash is an error at landing), duplicates within the units, and,
for information, the existing declarations that share a new declaration's last component in a
namespace that the new modules' consumers open together with `Turing` (the root `Turing`
namespace and `Complexity`), where an unqualified use could become ambiguous. With --list, also
writes the full names of the units' declarations, one per line (the axiom probe reads it).
"""
import os
import re
import sys

DECL = re.compile(r"^(?:@\[[^\]]*\]\s*)*(?:(?:private|protected|noncomputable|nonrec|partial)\s+)*"
                  r"(theorem|lemma|def|structure|abbrev|inductive|instance|class)\s+"
                  r"([A-Za-z0-9_.'«»₀-₉ᵢ-ᵪͰ-Ͽᴀ-ᶿ]+)")


def strip(src):
    out, i, depth = [], 0, 0
    while i < len(src):
        if depth == 0 and src.startswith("--", i):
            j = src.find("\n", i)
            i = len(src) if j < 0 else j
            continue
        if src.startswith("/-", i):
            depth += 1; i += 2; continue
        if src.startswith("-/", i) and depth > 0:
            depth -= 1; i += 2; continue
        if depth == 0:
            out.append(src[i])
        elif src[i] == "\n":
            out.append("\n")
        i += 1
    return "".join(out)


def decls(path):
    stack, res = [], []
    for line in strip(open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()).splitlines():
        if line.startswith(" "):
            continue
        s = line.strip()
        m = re.match(r"namespace\s+(\S+)", s)
        if m:
            stack += [("ns", p) for p in m.group(1).split(".")]
            continue
        m = re.match(r"(?:noncomputable\s+)?section\b\s*(\S*)", s)
        if m and s.split()[0] in ("section", "noncomputable"):
            stack.append(("sec", m.group(1)))
            continue
        m = re.match(r"end\b\s*(\S*)$", s)
        if m:
            nm = m.group(1)
            if nm:
                for p in reversed(nm.split(".")):
                    if stack and stack[-1][1] == p:
                        stack.pop()
            elif stack and stack[-1][0] == "sec":
                stack.pop()
            continue
        m = DECL.match(s)
        if m and m.group(1) != "instance":
            n = m.group(2)
            ns = [p for k, p in stack if k == "ns"]
            res.append(n[len("_root_."):] if n.startswith("_root_.") else ".".join(ns + [n]))
    return res


def main():
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    listing, replaced = None, set()
    if "--list" in args:
        k = args.index("--list"); listing = args[k + 1]; args = args[:k] + args[k + 2:]
    if "--replaces" in args:
        k = args.index("--replaces"); replaced = set(args[k + 1].split(","))
        args = args[:k] + args[k + 2:]
    units, root = args[:-1], args[-1]
    mine = [(n, os.path.basename(u)) for u in units for n in decls(u)]
    theirs = {}
    for d, _, fs in os.walk(os.path.join(root, "TCSlib")):
        for f in fs:
            if f.endswith(".lean"):
                p = os.path.join(d, f)
                for n in decls(p):
                    theirs.setdefault(n, []).append(os.path.relpath(p, root))
    print(f"{len(mine)} declarations in the units; {len(theirs)} distinct declaration names in "
          f"the worktree's TCSlib")
    full = [(n, u, theirs[n]) for n, u in mine if n in theirs and n not in replaced]
    for n in sorted(replaced):
        print(f"  replaced in place, as intended (not a clash): {n} {theirs.get(n)}")
    print(f"full-name clashes with TCSlib: {len(full)}")
    for n, u, w in full:
        print("  CLASH", n, u, w)
    names = [n for n, _ in mine]
    print("duplicates within the units:", sorted({n for n in names if names.count(n) > 1}))
    last = {}
    for n in theirs:
        last.setdefault(n.split(".")[-1], []).append(n)
    print("same last component, in `Turing` or `Complexity` directly (possible ambiguity under "
          "`open Turing` inside `namespace Complexity`):")
    hits = 0
    for n, _ in mine:
        for o in last.get(n.split(".")[-1], []):
            if o.count(".") == 1 and o.split(".")[0] in ("Turing", "Complexity") and o != n:
                print(f"  {n} ~ {o}"); hits += 1
    print(f"  ({hits})")
    print("same last component elsewhere (information; distinct namespaces):")
    for n, _ in mine:
        others = [o for o in last.get(n.split(".")[-1], []) if o != n]
        if others:
            print(f"  {n}: {', '.join(sorted(others)[:6])}{' …' if len(others) > 6 else ''}")
    if listing:
        open(listing, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(names) + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

## ===== audits/evidence/b6hosts/gate/scripts/cited.py =====

```
"""List the backticked tokens that look like declaration names (read-only).

Usage: python3 -I cited.py <file> [<file> ...]   (a `.patch` file contributes its added lines)
Prints each distinct token once, sorted.
"""
import re, sys
toks = set()
for p in sys.argv[1:]:
    src = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
    if p.endswith(".patch"):
        src = "\n".join(l[1:] for l in src.split("\n") if l.startswith("+") and not l.startswith("+++"))
    for t in re.findall(r"`([^`\n]+)`", src):
        t = t.strip()
        if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_'.?!₀-₉]*", t) and not t.endswith(".lean"):
            if "." in t or t[0].isupper() or "_" in t:
                toks.add(t)
for t in sorted(toks):
    print(t)
```

## ===== audits/evidence/b6hosts/gate/scripts/probes.py =====

```
"""Build the probe files from the current unit and patched files (read-only on the worktree).

Usage: python3 -I probes.py <outdir> <worktree>
Writes <outdir>/probes/Sanity.lean (the unit plus the sanity tail), the negative controls
<outdir>/work/neg<N>.lean (each a deliberately false copy of one probe), and
<outdir>/probes/GatedFormProbe.lean: the patched `Hierarchy.lean` in its patched import closure
(the cut check file) plus the gated statement of `space_universal`, extracted verbatim from the
worktree's `Hierarchy.lean` and renamed, proved from the strengthened theorem; and
<outdir>/probes/StepClockDraftFormProbe.lean: the unit plus the draft's statement of
`exists_stepClockTMVia`, extracted verbatim and renamed, proved from the landing form's.
"""
import os, sys
O, WT = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
def rd(p): return open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
def wr(p, s):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True); open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s)
unit = rd(os.path.join(O, "B6Hosts.lean"))
san = unit + rd(os.path.join(O, "scripts", "sanity_tail.lean"))
wr(os.path.join(O, "probes", "Sanity.lean"), san)
negs = [
    ("neg1", "example : summaryTag 1 (some true) = 2 := by decide",
     "example : summaryTag 1 (some true) = 1 := by decide"),
    ("neg2", "example : inputCell ([true] : List Bool) (2 - 1) ≠ none := by decide",
     "example : inputCell ([true] : List Bool) (2 - 1) = none := by decide"),
    ("neg3", "example : outSummaryCode (outSummary [true, true]) = 2 := by decide",
     "example : outSummaryCode (outSummary [true, true]) = 1 := by decide"),
    ("neg4", "example : (windowRun emitHalt 0 summaryTag 1 (emitHalt.initCfg []) 0).1 = .exhausted ∧",
     "example : (windowRun emitHalt 0 summaryTag 1 (emitHalt.initCfg []) 0).1 = .halted ∧"),
]
for name, a, b in negs:
    assert san.count(a) == 1, name
    wr(os.path.join(O, "work", name + ".lean"), san.replace(a, b))
# the gated statement, verbatim from the worktree
h = rd(os.path.join(WT, "TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/Hierarchy.lean"))
i = h.index("theorem space_universal :")
j = h.index(":= by", i)
stmt = h[i:j].replace("theorem space_universal :", "theorem space_universal_gated_form :", 1)
assert "C * (s + logSpace x.length + 1)" in stmt and stmt.count("space_universal") == 1
check = rd(os.path.join(O, "work", "cut", "Hierarchy.patched.check.lean"))
tail = """
/-! Probe (evidence only): the gated statement follows from the strengthened one. -/

namespace Complexity

open Turing

/-- **The strengthened `space_universal` implies the gated one** with the same machine and
constant: `C · s ≤ C · (s + logSpace |x| + 1)`. The statement is the gated `space_universal`
of the worktree, extracted verbatim and renamed. -/
""" + stmt + """:= by
  obtain ⟨SU, hSU⟩ := space_universal
  refine ⟨SU, fun α => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨C, hC, h⟩ := hSU α
  refine ⟨C, hC, fun s x output t h₁ h₂ => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨t', h₃, h₄⟩ := h s x output t h₁ h₂
  exact ⟨t', h₃, h₄.trans (Nat.mul_le_mul_left C (by omega))⟩

end Complexity
"""
wr(os.path.join(O, "probes", "GatedFormProbe.lean"), check.rstrip("\n") + "\n" + tail)
# the draft's statement of the step clock, verbatim, derived from the landing form's
d = rd(os.path.join(WT, "audits/evidence/b6hosts/B6HostsDraft.lean.txt"))
i = d.index("theorem exists_stepClockTMVia ")
j = d.index(":= by", i)
dstmt = d[i:j].replace("theorem exists_stepClockTMVia ", "theorem exists_stepClockTMVia_draft_form ", 1)
assert dstmt.count("exists_stepClockTMVia") == 1 and "Finset.Icc (cp - 1)" in dstmt
assert unit.count("theorem exists_stepClockTMVia ") == 1
sc = unit + """
/-! Probe (evidence only): the landing form's step clock implies the draft's statement, which the
C1 pack cites. The statement below is the draft's, extracted verbatim and renamed. -/

namespace Turing

""" + dstmt + """:= by
  obtain ⟨Q, hQ, dQ, H, inj, finish, timeout, h1, h2, h3, h4, h⟩ :=
    exists_stepClockTMVia e M stopAt
  refine ⟨Q, hQ, dQ, H, inj, finish, timeout, h1, h2, h3, h4, ?_⟩
  intro x c q hq w ct cp hw
  obtain ⟨hf, ht⟩ := h c q hq w ct cp hw
  refine ⟨fun τ hτ hs hm => ?_, fun hn => ?_⟩
  · obtain ⟨T, hT, w', hw', hr, hc, hfr⟩ := hf τ hτ hs hm
    refine ⟨T, hT, w', hw', hr, hc, fun u hu => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨v, hv, hj, -, -, hcp⟩ := hfr u hu
    exact ⟨v, hv, fun j => (hj j).2, hcp⟩
  · obtain ⟨T, hT, w', hw', hr, hc, hfr⟩ := ht hn
    refine ⟨T, hT, w', hw', hr, hc, fun u hu => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨v, hv, hj, -, -, hcp⟩ := hfr u hu
    exact ⟨v, hv, fun j => (hj j).2, hcp⟩

end Turing
"""
wr(os.path.join(O, "probes", "StepClockDraftFormProbe.lean"), sc)
print("probes, negative controls, the gated-form and the step-clock draft-form probes rebuilt;",
      "gated statement extracted:", len(stmt.splitlines()), "lines")

## ===== audits/evidence/b6hosts/gate/scripts/runall.sh =====

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Re-run every check of the B6 hosts statement gate and write the logs (read-only on the worktree).
# `lean` only through tools/leanelab.sh (no -o, no olean written); python3 -I for the scripts;
# `diff` and `patch` on scratch copies. No git, no lake.
# Usage: bash runall.sh <S>
S="$1"; WT="$S/wt-g5b6"; OL="$S/oleans-f8"; O="$S/gate-b6hosts"; SC="$O/scripts"; WK="$O/work"
LOGE="$O/elaboration.log"; LOGC="$O/cutcheck.log"; LOGF="$O/freeze.log"; LOGA="$O/axioms.log"
LOGN="$O/names.log"
el() { bash "$S/tools/leanelab.sh" "$WT" "$OL" "$1" 2>&1; }
san() { sed "s|$O/|<OUT>/|g; s|$S/|<S>/|g"; }
summ() { # output exit
  local e w s
  e=$(grep -c ': error' <<<"$1"); w=$(grep -c ': warning' <<<"$1")
  s=$(grep -c "declaration uses 'sorry'" <<<"$1")
  echo "exit $2 | errors $e | warnings $w | of which \`declaration uses 'sorry'\` $s | other warnings $((w - s))"
}
HEADC=$(cat /Users/seyoonr/phd_experiments/tcslib/.git/worktrees/wt-g5b6/HEAD)
prov() {
  echo "Tool: \`bash <S>/tools/leanelab.sh <S>/wt-g5b6 <S>/oleans-f8 <file>\` (a direct \`lean\` call"
  echo "inside the worktree, no \`-o\`, no olean written). Worktree: the read-only checkout \`wt-g5b6\`"
  echo "at campaign commit \`$HEADC\` (the worktree's HEAD file); olean snapshot \`oleans-f8\`"
  echo "(all of TCSlib at that commit, and Mathlib). Toolchain \`$(cat "$WT/lean-toolchain")\`."
  echo "<OUT> is this pack's scratch directory, <S> the scratchpad. Run: $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC')."
}
rm -rf "$WK/landing" "$WK/patched" "$WK/cut" "$WK/patchreplay"
mkdir -p "$O/patches" "$O/probes" "$WK"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- landing, patches, probes
LAND=$(cd "$SC" && python3 -I gate.py land "$O/B6Hosts.lean" "$WT" "$SC/edits.py" "$WK")
EXIST="TuringMachine/StateRenaming TuringMachine/Encoding SpaceComplexity/ConfigCount
TuringMachine/Build/CfgRecord SpaceComplexity/ConfigGraph SpaceComplexity/Hierarchy"
rm -f "$O"/patches/*.patch
for f in $EXIST; do
  b=$(basename "$f")
  (cd "$WT" && diff -u "TCSlib/Complexity/$f.lean" "$WK/patched/TCSlib/Complexity/$f.lean" |
    sed "1s|^--- .*|--- a/TCSlib/Complexity/$f.lean|; 2s|^+++ .*|+++ b/TCSlib/Complexity/$f.lean|") \
    > "$O/patches/$b.patch"
done
for f in TuringMachine SpaceComplexity; do
  (cd "$WT" && diff -u "TCSlib/Complexity/$f.lean" "$WK/patched/TCSlib/Complexity/$f.lean" |
    sed "1s|^--- .*|--- a/TCSlib/Complexity/$f.lean|; 2s|^+++ .*|+++ b/TCSlib/Complexity/$f.lean|") \
    > "$O/patches/facade-$f.patch"
done
rm -rf "$O/landing"; cp -R "$WK/landing" "$O/landing"
CUT=$(cd "$SC" && python3 -I gate.py cut "$O/B6Hosts.lean" "$WT" "$SC/edits.py" "$WK")
PROBES=$(cd "$SC" && python3 -I probes.py "$O" "$WT")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- cut checks
{
echo "# B6 hosts statement gate: cut checks"
echo; prov; echo
echo "## 1. Landing: the parts placed, the asserted edits applied"
echo
echo "\`python3 -I <OUT>/scripts/gate.py land <OUT>/B6Hosts.lean <S>/wt-g5b6 <OUT>/scripts/edits.py"
echo "<OUT>/work\` writes the five new modules (copyright, the part's imports, the standard options,"
echo "the part verbatim) and the eight patched existing files (each part placed as its header says,"
echo "then the edits of \`edits.py\`, each asserted to match exactly once)."
echo '```'; san <<<"$LAND"; echo '```'
echo
echo "## 2. Patch replay"
echo
echo "Each patch is applied with \`patch -p1\` to a scratch copy of the worktree file, and the result"
echo "is compared byte for byte with the patched file."
echo '```'
mkdir -p "$WK/patchreplay"
for p in "$O"/patches/*.patch; do
  t=$(sed -n '1s|^--- a/||p' "$p")
  mkdir -p "$WK/patchreplay/$(dirname "$t")"; cp "$WT/$t" "$WK/patchreplay/$t"
  (cd "$WK/patchreplay" && patch -s -p1 < "$p")
  if cmp -s "$WK/patchreplay/$t" "$WK/patched/$t"; then r=identical; else r=DIFFERENT; fi
  echo "$(basename "$p"): $t, $(grep -c '^+[^+]' "$p") added / $(grep -c '^-[^-]' "$p") removed lines; replay $r"
done
echo '```'
echo
echo "## 3. Each landing module in exactly its own import closure"
echo
echo "\`python3 -I <OUT>/scripts/gate.py cut …\` writes one check file per part and one per patched"
echo "existing file: the imports of the target and of the parts in its import closure, the standard"
echo "options, the bodies of those parts in file order, then the target's own body. The closure is"
echo "computed over the worktree's import graph, so an appended part is included wherever its module"
echo "is imported, directly or not. Part K (a replacement) is never included in another target."
echo '```'; san <<<"$CUT"; echo '```'
echo
for f in "$WK"/cut/*.check.lean; do

echo '```'

import os, sys
wt, unit = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
g = {}
for dp, _, fs in os.walk(os.path.join(wt, "TCSlib")):
    for f in fs:
        if f.endswith(".lean"):
            p = os.path.join(dp, f); m = os.path.relpath(p, wt)[:-5].replace(os.sep, ".")
            g[m] = [l.split()[1] for l in open(p, encoding="utf-8") if l.startswith("import TCSlib")]
parts, cur = {}, None
for l in open(unit, encoding="utf-8"):
    if l.startswith("-- @landing "): cur = l.split()[2]; parts[cur] = []
    elif l.startswith("-- @imports ") and cur: parts[cur] += l.split()[2:]
def clo(ms):
    seen, todo = set(), list(ms)
    while todo:
        m = todo.pop()
        if m in seen: continue
        seen.add(m); todo += parts.get(m, []) if m not in g else g[m]
    return seen
for m in parts:
    if m in g: continue
    c = clo(parts[m]); sc = sorted(x for x in c if ".SpaceComplexity." in x or x.endswith(".SpaceComplexity"))
    print(f"{m}: closure {len(c)} modules; SpaceComplexity modules: {len(sc)}{' ' + str(sc[:3]) + ' …' if sc else ''}")
PYEOF
echo '```'
} > "$LOGC"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- freeze
{
echo "# B6 hosts statement gate: freeze check of the eight existing files touched"
echo; prov; echo
echo "\`python3 -I <OUT>/scripts/freeze.py <worktree file> <patched file> <allowed statement changes>"
echo "<allowed body changes>\`: every declaration's statement (comment-stripped, up to the top-level"
echo "\`:=\`), body and docstring compared; a statement or body change outside the allowances fails."
echo "The allowances are exactly the user's decisions B1 (\`space_universal\`) and B3 (the S1b"

allow_s() { case "$1" in

  TuringMachine/Encoding) echo "Turing.exists_codeTM" ;;

for f in $EXIST; do

## ===== audits/evidence/b6hosts/gate/scripts/sanity_tail.lean.txt =====


/-! ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Sanity probes (evidence only; not landing material). Appended to a copy of the unit. -/

namespace B6HostsSanity

open Turing

/-! ### H5: the virtual input cell and the ruler device's facts, the empty payload included -/

example : inputCell ([] : List Bool) 0 = none := by decide
example : inputCell ([] : List Bool) 1 = none := by decide
example : inputCell [true, false] 1 = some true := by decide
example : inputCell [true, false] 2 = some false := by decide
example : inputCell [true, false] 3 = none := by decide

/-- The boundary test on `z = [true]` (a one-cell header, empty payload): at `p = ℓ = 1` the
probed cell is blank, at the right blank `p = 2 = |z| + 1` it is the header's cell. -/
example : inputCell ([true] : List Bool) (1 - 1) = none ↔ 1 = 1 :=
  inputCell_sub_eq_none_iff (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)
example : inputCell ([true] : List Bool) (2 - 1) = none ↔ 2 = 1 :=
  inputCell_sub_eq_none_iff (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)
example : inputCell ([true] : List Bool) (2 - 1) ≠ none := by decide

/-- Past the header of an empty payload the virtual cell is the physical right blank. -/
example : inputCell ([] : List Bool) 1 = inputCell [true, false] (2 + 1) :=
  inputCell_of_drop (z := [true, false]) (ℓ := 2) rfl (by decide)

/-- `space_universal`'s header for a one-bit budget word `[true]` (the value of `bits 1`), the
empty code and the empty payload: six cells, and nothing after them. -/
example : pairEncode [true] (pairEncode [] []) = [true, true, false, true, false, true] := by
  decide
example : (pairEncode [true] (pairEncode [] ([] : List Bool))).length =
    (2 * [true].length + 2 * ([] : List Bool).length + 4) + 0 :=
  pairEncode_pairEncode_length _ _ _
example : (pairEncode [true] (pairEncode [] ([] : List Bool))).drop
    (2 * [true].length + 2 * ([] : List Bool).length + 4) = [] :=
  pairEncode_pairEncode_drop _ _ _

/-- The native device presents the initial configuration at virtual position `1`. -/
example (y : List Bool) : NativeAt (Cfg.init () y : Cfg 2 Bool Unit y) 1 := nativeAt_init () y

/-! ### H3: the summary tag (accept is exactly `[true]`) -/

example : outSummaryCode (outSummary []) = 0 := by decide
example : outSummaryCode (outSummary [true]) = 1 := by decide
example : outSummaryCode (outSummary [true, true]) = 2 := by decide
example : outSummaryCode (outSummary [false]) = 2 := by decide
example : summaryTag 0 (some true) = 1 := by decide
example : summaryTag 0 (some false) = 2 := by decide
example : summaryTag 1 (some true) = 2 := by decide
example : summaryTag 1 none = 1 := by decide
example : summaryTag 2 (some true) = 2 := by decide
example : ¬ (outSummaryCode (outSummary [true, false]) = 1) := by decide

/-! ### H3: the windowed run on a machine that halts on its first transition, emitting `true`

The machine has no work tapes; the input is empty and the window radius is `0`. Its run halts
at time `1` by a transition that emits the deciding bit. One round is not enough (the clock is
exhausted, with the halted configuration); two rounds report `halted` with tag `1`. -/

/-- A machine with no work tapes that emits `true` and halts at its first transition. -/
def emitHalt : MultiTapeTM 0 Bool Unit where
  q₀ := ()
  tr := fun _ _ _ => ⟨0, Fin.elim0, some true, none⟩

theorem emitHalt_inWindow (c : Cfg 0 Bool Unit []) (s : ℕ) : c.InWindow s :=
  ⟨fun i => i.elim0, fun i => i.elim0⟩

theorem emitHalt_halts : (emitHalt.runFrom (emitHalt.initCfg []) 1).state = none := rfl

theorem emitHalt_emits : emitHalt.outputSymbol (emitHalt.runFrom (emitHalt.initCfg []) 0) =
    some true := rfl

/-- Clock exhaustion on the last transition: one round reports `exhausted`, at the halted
configuration of time `1`. -/
example : (windowRun emitHalt 0 summaryTag 1 (emitHalt.initCfg []) 0).1 = .exhausted ∧
    (windowRun emitHalt 0 summaryTag 1 (emitHalt.initCfg []) 0).2.1 =
      emitHalt.runFrom (emitHalt.initCfg []) 1 :=
  windowRun_exhausted_of_live emitHalt 0 summaryTag 1 _ 0
    (fun u hu => by rw [show u = 0 by omega]; simp [emitHalt, MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Cfg.init])
    (fun u _ => emitHalt_inWindow _ 0)

/-- The halt on the last transition with the deciding bit: two rounds report `halted` with the
tag of `[true]`, which is `1`. -/
example : windowRun emitHalt 0 summaryTag 2 (emitHalt.initCfg []) 0 =
    (.halted, emitHalt.runFrom (emitHalt.initCfg []) 1, 1) := by
  have h := windowRun_halts_on_last_transition emitHalt 0 summaryTag
    (fun u => outSummaryCode (outSummary u)) summaryTag_append 0 (emitHalt.initCfg []) true
    emitHalt_halts emitHalt_emits (fun u _ => emitHalt_inWindow _ 0)
  exact h

/-! ### H5: the ruler host's contract in use (the H2-S finding 2 interface)

The two directions a consumer needs, derived from `Turing.exists_rulerHostTM` alone: the host
halts with the source's output within `C · (ℓ + 1)` times the source's time, and it never halts
unless the source has (the exit cut and the lower bound `t ≤ t'`). -/

example {m : ℕ} {S : Type} [Fintype S] [DecidableEq S] (M : MultiTapeTM m Bool S) :
    ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Fintype Q) (_ : DecidableEq Q) (H : MultiTapeTM (m + 1) Bool Q)
      (inj : S → Bool → Q) (C : ℕ),
      ∀ {y z : List Bool} (ℓ : ℕ) (hz : z.length = ℓ + y.length), 0 < ℓ → z.drop ℓ = y →
      ∀ (rt : ℤ → Option Bool) (rp : ℤ),
        (∀ p : ℤ, -1 ≤ p → p ≤ (ℓ : ℤ) →
          rt (rp + p) = FinTM.bufferTape (List.replicate ℓ true) p) →
      ∀ (c : Cfg m Bool S y) (b : Bool), (b = true ↔ c.inputPos.val = 0) →
        (∀ t, (M.runFrom c t).state = none → ∃ t' ≤ C * (ℓ + 1) * t,
          (H.runFrom (rulerHostCfg ℓ hz (c.state.map fun q => inj q b) c rt rp) t').state =
              none ∧
            (H.runFrom (rulerHostCfg ℓ hz (c.state.map fun q => inj q b) c rt rp) t').output =
              (M.runFrom c t).output) ∧
        (∀ h, (H.runFrom (rulerHostCfg ℓ hz (c.state.map fun q => inj q b) c rt rp) h).state =
            none → ∃ τ ≤ h, (M.runFrom c τ).state = none) := by
  obtain ⟨Q, hQ, dQ, H, inj, C, -, hH⟩ := exists_rulerHostTM M
  refine ⟨Q, hQ, dQ, H, inj, C, ?_⟩
  intro y z ℓ hz hℓ hy rt rp hrt c b hb
  refine ⟨fun t ht => ?_, fun h hh => ?_⟩
  · obtain ⟨t', -, ht', ⟨b', -, hrun⟩, -⟩ := hH ℓ hz hℓ hy rt rp hrt c b hb t
    refine ⟨t', ht', ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [hrun]
      simp [rulerHostCfg, ht]
    · rw [hrun]
      rfl
  · obtain ⟨t', hlo, -, -, hcut, -⟩ := hH ℓ hz hℓ hy rt rp hrt c b hb (h + 1)
    by_contra hne
    push_neg at hne
    exact hcut (fun u hu => hne u (by omega)) h (by omega) hh

end B6HostsSanity

/-

import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ConfigGraph
import TCSlib.Complexity.TimeHierarchy.Diagonal
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.CodeSimulator

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# B6 hosts: the windowed runner, its step clock, the input devices and `U₀`

**Status: statement draft for a statement gate; not for landing as one file.** These are the
public contracts that the window route of `Complexity.space_hierarchy` needs
(`machine-library-design.md` §16b item 3, backlog RD-3). They are written read-only against
the campaign tip and meet the requirements of the RD-3 statement gate's findings
(`audits/b6-restatement-findings.md`: notes 7–8, rows 1 and 3, the numbered checks and the
suggested sanity obligations). **Every pure lemma below is proved. Every machine contract is
`sorry`** with its proof sketch. The proposed homes, the consumers and the open questions are
in `B6-hosts-design.md`.

## Design

* **Hosts first** (`policy.md` §1, design §14). The window route needs three hosts and a
  machine row: the windowed runner (H3), its clock, the input devices (H5), and the
  self-application universal machine `U₀` as a public row consuming the step block (H2).
* **H3 is split into a pure semantics, a clock and a loop.** `Turing.windowRun` is the
  semantic windowed run: round by round, test for a halted state, else step, else leave the
  window. `Turing.exists_windowLoopTM` realizes it without a clock. The clock is the
  **step-clocked runner** `Turing.exists_stepClockTMVia`, one countdown tick per physical body
  step, which the nondeterministic time hierarchy (C1) also needs (joint design, C1 note §3.3;
  C1's draft statement is its `Bool` instance `Turing.exists_stepClockTM`, proved from it).
  `Turing.exists_windowRunnerTM` is the loop under that clock, and
  `Turing.exists_configWindowRunnerTM` builds a configuration-count clock itself: it is what
  the diagonalizer cites.
* **The tag is generic**, with the output summary's `Fin 3` code (design §12.8a decision O4)
  as the instance `Turing.summaryTag`.
* **H5 presents a virtual input `y` inside a physical input `z`.** The native device is the
  identity (`Turing.NativeAt`). The bounded-prefix ruler device (`Turing.RulerAt`, the gate's
  row 1) keeps the physical head at `ℓ + i` and a unary ruler of the header length `ℓ`; it
  tests the virtual left boundary by a restoring sweep of `ℓ` cells. Its rows are call-level
  (`Turing.exists_rulerDeviceTM`), and `Turing.exists_rulerHostTM` turns any native-input
  machine into a ruler-hosted one, so that H2's block runs unchanged.
* **`U₀`** (`Turing.exists_selfUniversal`) is stated for any effective scheme. It is stated
  against H2's contract as delivered (`h1Round_effect`, private in
  `TuringMachine/CodeSimulator.lean`), whose assumptions are listed in its sketch.

## Main definitions

* `Turing.WindowExit`, `Turing.windowRun` — the three exits and the semantic windowed run.
* `Turing.outSummaryCode`, `Turing.summaryTag` — the output summary's `Fin 3` tag.
* `Turing.clockCfg`, `Turing.wordPatch`, `Turing.Cfg.Stopped` — the step clock's layout.
* `Turing.inputCell`, `Turing.NativeAt`, `Turing.RulerAt`, `Turing.rulerHostCfg` — the input
  device layer.

## Main results

* Bridges (proved): `Turing.MultiTapeTM.relabelState_spaceUsed`,
  `Turing.exists_codeTM_spaceUsed`, `Turing.CodeTM.one_le_spaceUsed`,
  `Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.spaceUsed_le_of_halt`,
  `Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace.computesFunInTime_and_forall_spaceUsed_le`,
  `Turing.FinTM.inWindow_of_spaceUsed_le`, `Turing.Cfg.inWindow_init`,
  `Turing.FinTM.decidesInSpace_of_alphabetReduction`.
* H3 semantics (proved): `Turing.windowRun_halted_of_run`, `Turing.windowRun_spec`,
  `Turing.windowRun_tag`, `Turing.windowRun_stop_unique`,
  `Turing.windowRun_exhausted_of_live`, `Turing.windowRun_halts_on_last_transition`,
  `Turing.summaryTag_append`, `Turing.windowRun_summary_of_halts`,
  `Turing.FinTM.configBound_le_two_pow`.
* H5 semantics (proved): `Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol_eq_inputCell`, `Turing.NativeAt.inputSymbol_eq`,
  `Turing.inputCell_sub_eq_none_iff`, `Turing.inputCell_of_drop`,
  `Turing.pairEncode_pairEncode_drop`.
* Host contracts (sorried): `Turing.exists_stepClockTMVia` (with C1's `Bool` form
  `Turing.exists_stepClockTM` proved from it), `Turing.exists_windowLoopTM`,
  `Turing.exists_windowRunnerTM`, `Turing.exists_configWindowRunnerTM`,
  `Turing.exists_rulerTestTM`, `Turing.exists_rulerDeviceTM`, `Turing.exists_rulerHostTM`,
  `Turing.exists_selfStartupTM`, `Turing.exists_selfUniversal`.
* The proposed addend-free `Complexity.B6Draft.space_universal` (sorried), and the proved
  `Complexity.B6Draft.space_universal_gated_form`: it implies the gated statement.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.2: the read-only input tape; §1.4.1, Theorem 1.9: the
  universal machine and its step; §3.2: the clocked simulations of the hierarchy proofs;
  §4.1.1, Claim 4.4: configurations and their count; §4.1.3, Theorem 4.8 and Exercise 4.1:
  the space hierarchy and the space-bounded universal machine.)
-/

namespace Turing

/-! ## §1 Bridges -/

/-- **State relabelling preserves every head trajectory.** For any machine `tm` and any state
equivalence `e`, head `i` of the relabelled machine visits, in its first `t` steps from its
initial configuration, exactly the cells that head `i` of `tm` visits. This is the space
clause that the coding step `Turing.exists_codeTM` does not state. [AB09, §1.4: the coding
step of the normal form]

**Proof sketch.** The relabelled run is the original run with its states renamed
(`Turing.MultiTapeTM.relabelState_runFrom_init`), and renaming changes no head position. -/
theorem MultiTapeTM.relabelState_visitedByTapeHead {k : ℕ} {Symbol : Type*}
    {State State' : Type*} (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State) (e : State ≃ State')
    (input : List Symbol) (t : ℕ) (i : Fin k) :
    (tm.relabelState e).visitedByTapeHead ((tm.relabelState e).initCfg input) t i =
      tm.visitedByTapeHead (tm.initCfg input) t i := by
  simp only [MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead, MultiTapeTM.relabelState_runFrom_init,
    Cfg.mapState]

/-- **State relabelling preserves space at every time.** The relabelled machine uses exactly
the space of the original up to every time `t`. [AB09, §1.4]

**Proof sketch.** Sum `Turing.MultiTapeTM.relabelState_visitedByTapeHead` over the tapes. -/
theorem MultiTapeTM.relabelState_spaceUsed {k : ℕ} {Symbol : Type*} {State State' : Type*}
    (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State) (e : State ≃ State') (input : List Symbol) (t : ℕ) :
    (tm.relabelState e).spaceUsed ((tm.relabelState e).initCfg input) t =
      tm.spaceUsed (tm.initCfg input) t := by
  simp only [MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, MultiTapeTM.spaceUsedByTape,
    MultiTapeTM.relabelState_visitedByTapeHead]

/-- **The space-faithful coding step.** Every one-work-tape binary machine `M` is equivalent
to a coded machine `M'` that halts with the same outputs at the same times
(`Turing.exists_codeTM`'s clause) **and uses the same space at every time**. This is the space
clause of the coding step named by `space_hierarchy`'s sketch. [AB09, §1.4]

**Proof sketch.** The witness of `Turing.exists_codeTM`: relabel the states along an
equivalence with `Fin (|Q| - 1 + 1)`. Its timed clause is that theorem's proof; the space
clause is `Turing.MultiTapeTM.relabelState_spaceUsed`. -/
theorem exists_codeTM_spaceUsed (M : FinTM Bool) (hk : M.k = 1) :
    ∃ M' : CodeTM,
      (∀ (x output : List Bool) (t : ℕ),
        M'.toFinTM.ComputesInTime x output t ↔ M.ComputesInTime x output t) ∧
      ∀ (x : List Bool) (t : ℕ),
        M'.toFinTM.tm.spaceUsed (M'.toFinTM.tm.initCfg x) t =
          M.tm.spaceUsed (M.tm.initCfg x) t := by
  classical
  rcases M with @⟨k, Q, hQ, dQ, tm⟩
  dsimp only at hk
  subst k
  letI : Fintype Q := hQ
  letI : DecidableEq Q := dQ
  have hcard : Fintype.card Q = (Fintype.card Q - 1) + 1 := by
    have : 0 < Fintype.card Q := Fintype.card_pos_iff.mpr ⟨tm.q₀⟩
    omega
  let e := Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq hcard
  refine ⟨⟨Fintype.card Q - 1, tm.relabelState e⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro x output t
    simp only [CodeTM.toFinTM, FinTM.ComputesInTime, MultiTapeTM.ComputesInTimeAndSpace,
      MultiTapeTM.relabelState_runFrom_init, Cfg.mapState, Option.map_eq_none_iff]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨s, hhalt, hout, -⟩
      exact ⟨_, hhalt, hout, rfl⟩
    · rintro ⟨s, hhalt, hout, -⟩
      exact ⟨_, hhalt, hout, rfl⟩
  · intro x t
    exact MultiTapeTM.relabelState_spaceUsed tm e x t

/-- **A coded run visits at least one cell.** Every run of a coded machine, at every time,
has visited at least one work cell: its one work head starts somewhere. So every qualifying
budget `s` of `space_universal` is positive (the gate's row-1 calculation).

**Proof sketch.** The visited set of tape `0` contains the head's initial position, and it
is one summand of the space. -/
theorem CodeTM.one_le_spaceUsed (M : CodeTM) (x : List Bool) (t : ℕ) :
    1 ≤ M.toFinTM.tm.spaceUsed (M.toFinTM.tm.initCfg x) t := by
  let i₀ : Fin M.toFinTM.k := ⟨0, by simp⟩
  have hne : (M.toFinTM.tm.visitedByTapeHead (M.toFinTM.tm.initCfg x) t i₀).Nonempty :=
    ⟨_, Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨0, Finset.mem_range.mpr (Nat.succ_pos t), rfl⟩⟩
  exact (Finset.card_pos.mpr hne).trans_le
    (M.toFinTM.tm.spaceUsedByTape_le_spaceUsed _ t i₀)

namespace FinTM

/-- **The halt-time space bound holds at every time.** If `M` has halted on `x` with output
`w` by time `t`, having visited at most `s` cells by then, it has visited at most `s` cells
by **every** time `t'`: before `t` by monotonicity, after `t` because the halted
configuration is frozen. This is the all-times bridge named by `space_hierarchy`'s sketch
(`DecidesInSpace` bounds the space at the halt; the normal form needs every time).

**Proof sketch.** Every head position visited by time `t'` was visited by time `t`: a time
`u ≤ t` is in range, and at a time `u > t` the configuration is the one at `t`
(`Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_of_halt`). So each visited set at `t'` is contained in the one at
`t`. -/
theorem ComputesInTime.spaceUsed_le_of_halt {Symbol : Type} {M : FinTM Symbol}
    {x w : List Symbol} {t s : ℕ} (h : M.ComputesInTime x w t)
    (hs : M.tm.spaceUsed (M.tm.initCfg x) t ≤ s) :
    ∀ t', M.tm.spaceUsed (M.tm.initCfg x) t' ≤ s := by
  have hhalt := ((computesInTime_iff M x w t).mp h).1
  have key : ∀ t' i, M.tm.visitedByTapeHead (M.tm.initCfg x) t' i ⊆
      M.tm.visitedByTapeHead (M.tm.initCfg x) t i := by
    intro t' i z hz
    simp only [MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead, Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_range] at hz ⊢
    obtain ⟨u, hu, rfl⟩ := hz
    by_cases hut : u ≤ t
    · exact ⟨u, by omega, rfl⟩
    · refine ⟨t, by omega, ?_⟩
      rw [show u = t + (u - t) by omega, MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add,
        MultiTapeTM.runFrom_of_halt _ hhalt]
  intro t'
  refine le_trans ?_ hs
  exact Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => Finset.card_le_card (key t' i)

/-- **A space-bounded computation in the normal form's hypotheses.** If `M` computes `f`
within space `s`, then it computes `f` within the length-dependent time
`n ↦ configBound M n (s n)`, and its space is at most `s |x|` at every time on every `x`.
These are exactly the hypotheses `hM` and `hS` of
`Turing.FinTM.one_work_tape_binary_spaceUsed`. [AB09, §4.1.1]

**Proof sketch.** Time: `Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.of_spaceUsed_le`. Space at every time:
`Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.spaceUsed_le_of_halt`. -/
theorem ComputesInSpace.computesFunInTime_and_forall_spaceUsed_le {M : FinTM Bool}
    {f : List Bool → List Bool} {s : ℕ → ℕ} (h : M.ComputesInSpace f s) :
    M.ComputesFunInTime f (fun n => M.configBound n (s n)) ∧
      ∀ (x : List Bool) (t : ℕ), M.tm.spaceUsed (M.tm.initCfg x) t ≤ s x.length := by
  refine ⟨fun x => ?_, fun x t => ?_⟩
  · obtain ⟨t, ht, hsp⟩ := h x
    exact ht.of_spaceUsed_le hsp
  · obtain ⟨t₀, ht, hsp⟩ := h x
    exact ht.spaceUsed_le_of_halt hsp t

/-- **Window containment.** If `M` has visited at most `s` work cells by time `t` on `x`,
then every configuration of its run up to time `t` lies in the radius-`s` window: every head
is within `[-s, s]` and every cell outside it is blank. This is the containment step of
`space_hierarchy`'s contradiction, and the hypothesis under which the windowed runner follows
the run. [AB09, §4.1.1, Claim 4.4]

**Proof sketch.** Each tape's visited set has at most `s` cells and is an interval around `0`
(`Turing.MultiTapeTM.abs_pos_lt_card_visited`), so each visited cell has absolute value below
`s`. The head at time `u` is visited, and a nonblank cell at time `u` was visited by then
(`Turing.MultiTapeTM.mem_visited_of_ne_none`), hence by time `t`. -/
theorem inWindow_of_spaceUsed_le (M : FinTM Bool) (x : List Bool) {t s : ℕ}
    (hs : M.tm.spaceUsed (M.tm.initCfg x) t ≤ s) :
    ∀ u ≤ t, (M.tm.runFrom (M.tm.initCfg x) u).InWindow s := by
  intro u hu
  have hmem : ∀ i, ∀ z ∈ M.tm.visitedByTapeHead (M.tm.initCfg x) t i, |z| < (s : ℤ) := by
    intro i z hz
    have hcard : (M.tm.visitedByTapeHead (M.tm.initCfg x) t i).card ≤ s :=
      (M.tm.spaceUsedByTape_le_spaceUsed _ t i).trans hs
    exact (M.tm.abs_pos_lt_card_visited x t i hz).trans_le (by exact_mod_cast hcard)
  refine ⟨fun i => (hmem i _ ?_).le, fun i z hz => ?_⟩
  · simp only [MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead, Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_range]
    exact ⟨u, by omega, rfl⟩
  · by_contra hne
    have hv := M.tm.visitedByTapeHead_mono _ hu i (M.tm.mem_visited_of_ne_none x u i z hne)
    have := hmem i z hv
    omega

/-- **The initial configuration is in every window**: its heads are at `0` and its work
tapes are blank. The windowed runner's precondition at the start of `space_hierarchy`'s
simulation.

**Proof sketch.** Unfold `Cfg.init`. -/
